### FrontView REIT Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results


November 4, 2026


- [Download (opens in new window)](https://s205.q4cdn.com/268754373/files/doc_news/FrontView-REIT-Announces-Third-Quarter-2026-Results-2026.pdf)


DALLAS--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


FrontView REIT, Inc. (NYSE: FVR) (the “Company,” “FrontView,” “we,” “our,” or “us”), today announced its operating results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.


**MANAGEMENT COMMENTARY**


“FrontView delivered AFFO per share of $0.33 and acquired 16 properties at a 7.6% cap rate during the quarter. Our size, granular portfolio and differentiated acquisition strategy provide structural advantages in a market with limited institutional competition. We continue to source high-quality real estate at increasingly attractive investment spreads, with acquisition yields expected to move higher in the fourth quarter. Combined with the organic growth potential embedded in our portfolio, these opportunities position FrontView to compound earnings and create long-term shareholder value. We intend to capitalize on this environment, maintain our acquisition momentum and expect to meet or exceed our full-year net investment guidance,” said Stephen Preston, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of FrontView REIT.


**THIRD QUARTER 2026 HIGHLIGHTS**


- Generated net income of $3.0 million, or $0.08 per share with funds from operations (“FFO”) of $7.4 million, or $0.25 per share and adjusted funds from operations (“AFFO”) of $9.7 million, or $0.33 per share.
- Acquired 16 properties for $50.6 million at an average capitalization rate of 7.56% and a weighted average lease term of 6.4 years.
- Sold 5 occupied properties for $17.1 million in gross proceeds with an average capitalization rate of 6.56% and a weighted average lease term of 6.4 years.
- Strong liquidity with $174.0 million in capacity between cash and cash equivalents, availability under our revolving credit facility and undrawn Series A Convertible Preferred Stock.
- Maintained strong operational performance, including 99.4% occupancy.
- During the third quarter, we sold 9,373 shares of common stock on a forward basis under the Company’s at-the-market equity offering program at a weighted average gross price of $21.01 per share, generating gross proceeds of approximately $0.2 million. We issued and settled 1,699,165 shares of common stock that were sold on a forward basis under the Company's at-the-market equity offering program for proceeds of $32.7 million.
- Lowered leverage with Net Debt to Annualized Adjusted EBITDAre falling to 5.0x, Adjusted Net Debt to Annualized Adjusted EBITDAre of 4.5x, and leverage ratio of 30.6%.
- Paid a quarterly dividend per common share of $0.215 representing an AFFO per share payout ratio of 64.7%.

**DISTRIBUTIONS**


On November 3, 2026, our board of directors authorized a quarterly dividend of $0.215 per common share and a quarterly distribution of $0.215 per OP unit, each payable in cash on January 15, 2027, to holders of record as of December 31, 2026.


On November 3, 2026, our board of directors authorized a regular quarterly dividend on the Series A Convertible Preferred Stock, payable in cash on January 15, 2027, to holders of record as of December 31, 2026. As of November 3, 2026, 383,333 shares of Series A Convertible Preferred Stock were issued and outstanding.


**PROMOTION ANNOUNCEMENT**


On November 3, 2026, our board of directors promoted Pierre Revol, our Chief Financial Officer, Treasurer, and Secretary, to become a President of the Company, effective November 3, 2026. Following his promotion, Mr. Revol’s title is President, Chief Financial Officer, Treasurer and Secretary.


**2026 GUIDANCE**


The Company is maintaining its full year 2026 AFFO per share guidance range of $1.32 to $1.34 and its net investment activity of approximately $120.0 million.


The Company's 2026 guidance is based on a number of assumptions that are subject to change and many of which are outside the Company's control. If actual results vary from these assumptions, the Company's expectations may change. There can be no assurance that the Company will achieve these results.


We do not provide guidance for the most comparable GAAP financial measure, net income, or a reconciliation of the forward-looking non-GAAP financial measure of AFFO per share to earnings per share attributable to common stockholders computed in accordance with GAAP, because we are unable to reasonably predict, without unreasonable efforts, certain items that would be contained in the GAAP measure, including items that are not indicative of our ongoing operations, including, without limitation, potential impairments of real estate assets, net gain/loss on dispositions of real estate assets, changes in allowance for credit losses, and stock-based compensation expense. These items are uncertain, depend on various factors, and could have a material impact on our GAAP results for the guidance periods.

**About FrontView REIT, Inc.**


FrontView is an internally managed net-lease real estate investment trust (“REIT”) focused on acquiring, owning, and managing properties with frontage that are leased to a diversified tenant base. Our real estate-first investment strategy is centered around highly visible properties in prominent retail corridors with strong underlying real estate fundamentals. We target properties along high-traffic roads that offer strong consumer visibility and adaptable building formats capable of supporting various businesses over time.


As of September 30, 2026, FrontView owned a diversified portfolio of 327 direct frontage properties across 36 U.S. states, leased primarily to service and necessity based tenants across 16 industries, including medical and dental providers, quick-service and casual dining restaurants, financial institutions, cellular retailers, automotive related, fitness, and general retail along with several other diversified industries.

FFO is computed in accordance with the definition adopted by Nareit: net income (loss) excluding real estate depreciation and amortization, gains (losses) on sales of depreciated real estate, gains and losses from change in control, and impairments of depreciated real estate. FFO is widely used by REITs because real estate depreciation assumes property values decline predictably over time, while real estate values have historically risen or fallen with market conditions.


AFFO is FFO further adjusted to exclude non-cash revenues and expenses and items we do not consider part of our ongoing operations: straight-line rent, amortization of above/below-market lease intangibles, amortization of debt issuance costs, non-cash stock-based compensation, structuring and public company readiness costs, and other non-recurring expenses such as deal pursuit costs. Because our leases have contractual rent escalations and generally no significant free-rent periods, we believe AFFO better reflects the recurring cash earnings generated by our portfolio and our capacity to pay dividends. Adjustments for the unconsolidated entity are calculated on the same basis.


We believe FFO and AFFO help investors compare our operating performance across periods and with other REITs. They should not be considered alternatives to net income or cash flows from operating activities and may not be comparable to similarly titled measures of other REITs.

EBITDA is net income before interest, income taxes and depreciation and amortization; EBITDAre, as defined by Nareit, further excludes gains (losses) on sales of depreciable property and real estate impairments. The unconsolidated entity is reflected on the same basis. Adjusted EBITDAre further (i) reflects quarterly investments and dispositions as if completed on the first day of the quarter and excludes (ii) infrequent or unusual items, (iii) lease termination fees from certain of our tenants and (iv) non-cash stock-based compensation.


Annualized Adjusted EBITDAre is quarterly Adjusted EBITDAre multiplied by four. We believe these measures are useful indicators of operating performance and current run rate; they are not alternatives to net income or operating cash flows, may not be comparable to other companies’ measures, and actual results may differ from annualized amounts.


Adjusted NOI is Adjusted EBITDAre excluding general and administrative expenses and adjustments for the unconsolidated entity. Adjusted Cash NOI is Adjusted NOI further adjusted for non-cash revenue items, including straight-line rent and other amortization.


Annualized Adjusted NOI and Annualized Adjusted Cash NOI are the applicable quarterly amounts multiplied by four. We believe these measures are useful because they reflect only property-level income and expenses, and the annualized measures provide a meaningful estimate of our current run rate given our long-term net leases. These measures should not be considered alternatives to net income or cash flows from operating activities, may not be comparable to similarly titled measures of other companies, and actual results may differ significantly from annualized amounts.

Net Debt is a non-GAAP financial measure. We define Net Debt as our Gross Debt less cash and cash equivalents. We then adjust Net Debt by the undrawn Series A Convertible Preferred Stock and unsettled forward equity to derive Adjusted Net Debt. The ratios of Net Debt to Annualized Adjusted EBITDAre and Adjusted Net Debt to Annualized Adjusted EBITDAre represent Net Debt and Adjusted Net Debt as of the end of the applicable period divided by Annualized Adjusted EBITDAre for the period, respectively. We believe that these ratios are useful to investors and analysts because they provide information about Gross Debt less cash and cash equivalents as well as Gross Debt less cash and cash equivalents, undrawn Series A Convertible Preferred Stock and unsettled forward equity, which could be useful to repay debt.
